caption: Figure 1: Different finetuning methods and their memory requirements. QLORA improves over LoRA by quantizing the transformer model to 4-bit precision and using paged optimizers to handle memory spikes.
description:
Description: The figure compares three fine-tuning methods for large language models: Full Finetuning, LoRA, and QLoRA. Full Finetuning uses 32-bit optimizer state and 16-bit adapters. LoRA uses 16-bit transformers. QLoRA quantizes the transformers to 4-bit and uses paged optimizers.

Text in figure: Full Finetuning, LoRA, QLoRA, Optimizer State, 32 bit, Adapters, 16 bit, Base Model, 16-bit Transformer, 16-bit Transformer, 4-bit Transformer, Parameter Updates, Gradient Flow, Paging Flow

caption: Figure 2: RougeL for LLaMA 7B models on the Alpaca dataset. Each point represents a run with a different random seed. We improve on the Stanford Alpaca fully finetuned default hyperparameters to construct a strong 16-bit baseline for comparisons. Using LoRA on all transformer layers is critical to match 16-bit performance.
description:
This figure is a scatter plot comparing the RougeL scores of various LLaMA 7B models on the Alpaca dataset. The x-axis represents different models, and the y-axis shows the RougeL score. The blue dots represent 4-bit models, and the orange dots represent 16-bit models. The highest score is achieved by the 16-bit Stanford-Alpaca model, while the lowest score is achieved by the 4-bit QLoRA-All model.

Text in figure: "RougeL", "4 bits", "16 bits", "QLoRA-All", "QLoRA-FFN", "QLoRA-Attention", "Alpaca (ours)", "Stanford-Alpaca"

caption: Figure 3: Mean zero-shot accuracy over Winogrande, HellaSwag, PiQA, Arc-Easy, and ArcChallenge using LLaMA models with different 4-bit data types. The NormalFloat data type significantly improves the bit-for-bit accuracy gains compared to regular 4-bit Floats. While Double Quantization (DQ) only leads to minor gains, it allows for a more fine-grained control over the memory footprint to fit models of certain size (33B/65B) into certain GPUs (24/48GB).
description:
Description: The figure is a line graph comparing mean zero-shot accuracy of LLaMA models with different 4-bit data types. The series labeled "Float" is the lowest, followed by "NFloat", and "NFloat + DQ" is the highest. The "NFloat + DQ" series peaks at around 0.67, while "Float" remains below 0.66.

Text in figure: "4-bit LLaMA", "Mean zero-shot accuracy", "Data type", "Float", "NFloat", "NFloat + DQ", "10^10", "10^11", "Total model bits".

caption: Figure 4: LoRA r for LLaMA 7B models finetuned on Alpaca. Each dot represents a combination of hyperparameters and for each LoRA r we run 3 random seed with each hyperparameter combination. The performance of specific LoRA r values appears to be independent of other hyperparameters.
description:
Figure 4 displays a scatter plot showing the performance of LLaMA 7B models finetuned on Alpaca with varying LoRA r values. Each dot represents a combination of hyperparameters, with three random seeds for each LoRA r value. The performance metric, RougeL, ranges from approximately 64.0 to 65.0. The plot indicates that the performance of specific LoRA r values is independent of other hyperparameters.

Text in figure: LoRA r, RougeL, bits, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 64.0, 64.2, 64.4, 64.6, 64.8, 65.0.

caption: Figure 5: The crowdsourcing form used by human annotators.
description:
Section 1: Figure type and content summary
This is a form used for collecting human feedback on the performance of two AI assistants. It includes a user question, two AI responses, and a rating scale for each response. The form also asks for a comprehensive explanation of the evaluation.

Section 2: Figure details
User Question: Imagine you are a time traveler from the year 3000. What technological advancements would you tell people about?
Response A: As an AI assistant, I don't have personal experiences or opinions. But I can tell you about some of the possible technological advancements that might exist in the year 3000 based on current trends and research.
Response B: As a time traveler from the year 3000, I would tell people about the following technological advancements: 1. Advanced Artificial Intelligence: In the future, AI is so advanced that it can completely automate many jobs that humans currently do. This has resulted in increased productivity and efficiency across many industries.
Rating scale: 1 to 10, where 1 is the lowest and 10 is the highest.

caption: Figure 6: Breakdown of the memory footprint of different LLaMA models. The input gradient size is for batch size 1 and sequence length 512 and is estimated only for adapters and the base model weights (no attention). Numbers on the bars are memory footprint in MB of individual elements of the total footprint. While some models do not quite fit on certain GPUs, paged optimzier provide enough memory to make these models fit.
description:
Description: This figure is a bar chart showing the memory footprint breakdown of different LLaMA models. The chart displays the memory usage for input gradient, optimizer, weight gradient, adapters, and the model itself. The model series is the highest, followed by the input gradient, optimizer, weight gradient, and adapters. The memory footprint for the 65B model is the largest, followed by 33B, 13B, and 7B.
